institutions.name: the Temple District
institutions.title: High Priest
institutions.blurb: The temple and the shrines around it, with their almshouses, pilgrims' hostels and processions. The council decides which god's house gets the best ground and the council's coin, and that god's blessing falls on the town.

choice.label: which god the district honours first
choice.text: Whichever god gets the best ground and the council's coin blesses the town in its own way.

options.name: the Lantern Mother's healers
options.text: Her infirmary opens beside the temple: heroes come home from the wilds and are on their feet in days.

options.name: Sylvaine's harvest rites
options.text: Her priests walk the furrows each dawn: the fields and herb beds bear more.

options.name: Haldor's forge-chapel
options.text: The Anvil-Father's priests bless every hammer in town: tools come truer and buildings go up faster.

options.name: Ostrava's watch-chapel
options.text: Her priests bless the walls and the watch every dusk: the town is harder to take.

options.name: Nim's counting-house shrine
options.text: Merchants leave coins in Nim's bowl for luck, and the luck seems to stick: trade is good.

keepers.name: Ilse Varrow
keepers.text: A battlefield surgeon before she took vows, she still keeps a bone saw on the altar and has no patience for sermons.

keepers.name: Tobin Ashgrove
keepers.text: Round, kind and endlessly in debt to the temple's cook, he knows every widow in town by name and every miser by his excuses.

keepers.name: Mere Hollin
keepers.text: Blind since a fever in her girlhood, she hears confessions in the dark and says she can smell a lie.

institutions.name: the Adventurers' Hall
institutions.title: Hallmaster
institutions.blurb: Where companies register, read the contract board and gear up. Contract fees pay the town a little, and the hall's specialty shapes what its members are good for.

choice.label: what the hall is known for
choice.text: A hall gets a name for one kind of work, and draws the companies who do it.

options.name: treasure seekers
options.text: The hall takes a cut of every haul registered at its counter, and the council takes a cut of the hall's.

options.name: monster hunters
options.text: Trophy heads go up over the door. The companies who come hunt what prowls near the walls.

options.name: road wardens
options.text: Hall members ride with the caravans: fewer are waylaid on the road.

options.name: rescuers
options.text: Hall members bring back the lost and the wounded. Heroes heal faster between delves.

keepers.name: Brask Dunmore
keepers.text: A one-handed former delver who keeps the contract board in a hand so neat no one believes he wrote it, and fines anyone who spits on his floor.

keepers.name: Yeva Quell
keepers.text: A retired scout with a ledger for a memory: she can tell you which company owes which, and who is lying about a ruin.

keepers.name: Old Corrin Tarth
keepers.text: Seventy and still sharpening other people's swords, he sends every new company out with the same advice: come back.

institutions.name: the Grand Bazaar
institutions.title: Bazaar Warden
institutions.blurb: A caravanserai with stalls for visiting merchants and lodging for their beasts. The town can run one more trade route, and the warden decides which far-off traders get the best pitches.

choice.label: which merchants the bazaar invites
choice.text: There are only so many pitches under the awnings, and each kind of trader brings its own crowd.

options.name: weavers of enchanted silks
options.text: Bolts of cloth that never fade: the gentry flock, and the looms in town learn their tricks.

options.name: dealers in rare metals
options.text: Ingots from the deep holds: the smiths make better tools.

options.name: spice and incense caravans
options.text: The streets smell of far lands, and travellers come to see what the fuss is about.

options.name: sellers of monster eggs and curios
options.text: Strange cages and stranger buyers. It pays well, and the Quiet Hand takes a keen interest.

keepers.name: Saffi Delacorte
keepers.text: A merchant prince's daughter who ran away to the caravan roads, she haggles in six tongues and never pays the first price for anything.

keepers.name: Umar Kesh
keepers.text: A former caravan master with a ruined knee, he still rises before dawn to count the camels in and knows every road by its bandits.

keepers.name: Goodwife Pell Ambry
keepers.text: Once a market-wife in the old town, she rules the bazaar like a kitchen: loud, fair, and with a ladle within reach.

institutions.name: the Druid Grove
institutions.title: Grove Warden
institutions.blurb: A patch of living wilderness inside the town: an ancient tree, a sacred pool and the druids who tend them. The fields bear more, the air is sweeter, and the grove has its own opinions.

choice.label: what the grove's druids tend first
choice.text: There are few druids and much to do: the council asks them to put one thing first.

options.name: the fields
options.text: The druids walk the furrows and the orchards: the harvest is richer.

options.name: healing plants
options.text: Herb beds spread through the grove: remedies are plentiful and wounds close faster.

options.name: speaking with the wild
options.text: The druids parley with the spirits of the woods around the town: the wilds are a little less hostile.

options.name: the waters
options.text: The streams through town run clean and cold: people are healthier, and settlers notice.

keepers.name: Wren Alderhusk
keepers.text: A druid who speaks to people as if they were slow-growing trees: kindly, patiently, and with no expectation they will understand.

keepers.name: Mossback Tull
keepers.text: Nobody is sure how old he is. He sleeps in the roots of the great tree and wakes when someone drops litter.

keepers.name: Teodora Fernlight
keepers.text: Young, fierce and newly sworn to the grove, she argues with the council as if every felled tree were a personal insult, which it is.

institutions.name: the town's famous tavern
institutions.title: Proprietor
institutions.blurb: The oldest tavern in town, grown famous: where rumours land, companies form and odd visitors come asking for help. Its style decides who drinks there.

choice.label: what kind of house the tavern keeps
choice.text: A tavern can be one thing well. The council's licence says which.

options.name: a comfortable inn for travellers
options.text: Feather beds and clean linen: merchants and wealthy travellers stay, and spend.

options.name: a rowdy adventurers' pub
options.text: Arm wrestling, war stories and a wall of notices: more heroes stop in town, and some stay.

options.name: a mysterious house for strange folk
options.text: Hooded guests, low lamps and a door that is never quite locked: the Quiet Hand drinks here, and so do stranger things.

keepers.name: Marta Kettleby
keepers.text: Three husbands buried, two taverns burned and one standing: she pours with one hand and holds a cudgel with the other.

keepers.name: Fenwick Brae
keepers.text: A failed bard who learned that people pay better to talk than to listen, he remembers every story told at his bar and sells the best ones back.

keepers.name: Hobb Underbough
keepers.text: A halfling with a laugh you can hear from the gate, who has never once been seen to sleep, and keeps a book of debts he never collects.

institutions.name: the Wizards' Library
institutions.title: Loremaster
institutions.blurb: The town's library, grown into a house of wizards: reading rooms, a warded vault for the spellbooks, and the wizards the books draw to town. The council decides which school the wizards put first, and the library's keeper speeds the scholars' work.

choice.label: which school the wizards put first
choice.text: The wizards are few and the books many: the council asks them to bend their work to one school.

options.name: wards on the walls
options.text: The wizards ring the town with wards that flare at night: raiders find the walls harder to take.

options.name: hands that build
options.text: Unseen servants haul stone and timber for the builders: every building goes up faster.

options.name: the alchemists' rooms
options.text: The wizards turn their art to the workshops: tools come truer and herbs keep longer.

options.name: the scrying rooms
options.text: The wizards watch the roads in their mirrors and warn the caravans: fewer are waylaid.

keepers.name: Orsolya Venn
keepers.text: A wizard who lost a hand to a book that bit and now keeps every grimoire in a cage, including the friendly ones.

keepers.name: Pell Quillan
keepers.text: Young, nervous and brilliant, he reads three books at once and remembers all of them, but never where he left his spectacles.

keepers.name: Dame Hester Coil
keepers.text: She was court wizard to a baron who died badly, and will not say how. She runs the library like a garrison.

institutions.name: the Paladin Chapterhouse
institutions.title: Knight-Commander
institutions.blurb: A fortified hall where an order of paladins keeps its vigil, trains its squires and judges its own. Its oath shapes what the knights do for the town, and a knight who breaks it is the town's problem too.

choice.label: the oath the chapter swears
choice.text: Every chapter swears one oath above the others, and the town lives with what it means.

options.name: the oath of devotion
options.text: The knights tend the sick and walk the night streets with lanterns: wounds heal and folk sleep easier.

options.name: the oath of vengeance
options.text: The knights swear to hunt every raider to its den: the wilds fear the town a little more.

options.name: the oath of the green
options.text: The knights guard the fields and orchards as if they were shrines: the harvest is safer and sweeter.

options.name: the oath of the crown
options.text: The knights swear to the town's law before their own conscience: the streets are orderly, if stern.

keepers.name: Dame Aveline Thorne
keepers.text: Forty years in the saddle and three horses buried, she still rises at the third bell to pray and expects her knights to do the same.

keepers.name: Ser Corwin Halloway
keepers.text: A reformed sellsword who found his god in a burning village, he is gentle with the weak and terrifying to everyone else.

keepers.name: Brother-Captain Joss Mallory
keepers.text: Young for his rank and painfully earnest, he keeps a ledger of every promise the town has ever made him.

institutions.name: the Alchemists' Quarter
institutions.title: Master Alchemist
institutions.blurb: A crooked lane of stills, kilns and coloured smoke where alchemists brew for the town. Potions and dyes flow out; now and then so does something that was meant to stay in the jar.

choice.label: what the quarter brews most
choice.text: Every still in the quarter can brew anything, given time. The council's coin decides what they brew first.

options.name: healing draughts
options.text: Red bottles by the crate: heroes come home sooner and fewer die of their wounds.

options.name: alchemist's fire
options.text: Clay pots of sticky flame stacked by the walls: the watch has something to throw.

options.name: dyes and perfumes
options.text: Madder reds and saffron yellows: the weavers' cloth sells further and dearer.

options.name: elixirs of youth
options.text: Very expensive, very popular and very slightly poisonous: the gold pours in.

keepers.name: Odo Brimwick
keepers.text: Eyebrowless since an accident he will not discuss, he tastes every batch himself and has outlived two apprentices who did not.

keepers.name: Sabeth Quill
keepers.text: She left the wizards' college over a matter of principle and a small fire, and has been proving them wrong ever since.

keepers.name: Old Mother Tansy
keepers.text: A herb-wife who learned her letters at sixty, she keeps her formulae in rhymes and her coin under a loose brick.

institutions.name: the Artificers' Foundry
institutions.title: Forgemaster
institutions.blurb: Furnaces, lathes and a great water-wheel, where artificers build clockwork, engines and the odd marvel. Better tools and faster building, and inventions with minds of their own.

choice.label: what the foundry builds
choice.text: The artificers can build anything the council can pay for. What they build first shapes the town.

options.name: clockwork labourers
options.text: Brass porters and stone-lifting engines: every building in town goes up faster.

options.name: engines of war
options.text: Ballistae on the towers and a springal at the gate: the walls bite back.

options.name: lamps and pumps
options.text: Clockwork pumps and everburning lamps in every street: life is easier and the nights brighter.

options.name: wonders for sale
options.text: Singing birds of silver and self-turning spits for rich men's kitchens: the merchants pay handsomely.

keepers.name: Ingra Coppervein
keepers.text: A dwarf who left her clan's forges for wanting to build things that move, she talks to her machines and claims they listen.

keepers.name: Pell Fennimore
keepers.text: A gnome of boundless enthusiasm and very few finished projects, he has patented the same kettle three times.

keepers.name: Master Hollis Grane
keepers.text: Grey, precise and humourless, he lost a hand to a steam valve and replaced it with a better one.

institutions.name: the Grand Arena
institutions.title: Arena Master
institutions.blurb: The city's arena under a master of games: duels, beasts and races before roaring crowds. It keeps the city cheerful and its coffers full, and every so often someone wants to fight to the death.

choice.label: what fills the arena
choice.text: The crowds come for anything bloody or fast. The council decides which.

options.name: heroes' duels
options.text: The town's champions spar for glory: travellers come to see a real hero fight.

options.name: beast fights
options.text: Owlbears and bulettes dragged from the wilds and killed before the crowd: the wilds seem less fearsome.

options.name: chariot races
options.text: Four teams, four colours, and wagers on all of them: a river of gold.

options.name: trials by combat
options.text: Grudges settled with blunted blades instead of knives in alleys: the streets are calmer.

keepers.name: Varro Stake
keepers.text: A retired gladiator with a voice like a landslide, he knows every fighter's weakness and every bookmaker's price.

keepers.name: Lady Ismene Corr
keepers.text: A noblewoman who bought the games to annoy her family, she runs them with a fan in one hand and a ledger in the other.

keepers.name: Grumm One-Tusk
keepers.text: A half-orc who fought in the pits as a boy, he insists every fighter is paid and every beast is fed.

institutions.name: the Bards' College
institutions.title: Dean of Bards
institutions.blurb: The theatre becomes a college of bards: players, poets and loremasters who sing the town's deeds and keep its memory. What they sing about decides how the town sees itself, and what the world hears of it.

choice.label: what the college sings
choice.text: Bards will sing anything. The town will believe what they sing most.

options.name: the deeds of the town's heroes
options.text: Ballads of every delve and duel: heroes walk taller, and more come looking for the town in the songs.

options.name: the old histories
options.text: Lays of the fallen kingdoms: the town's scholars learn faster, and its people know their place in the world.

options.name: satires of the powerful
options.text: Nobody is safe from the stage, the mayor least of all: folk laugh instead of riot.

options.name: songs of love
options.text: Every tavern hums the season's tune: the town is a happier place to live.

keepers.name: Lysander Vale
keepers.text: Once the most famous voice in the Free Ports, now hoarse and vain, he teaches as if every pupil were his last chance at an encore.

keepers.name: Mistress Oona Fairweather
keepers.text: A halfling loremaster who has memorised four thousand verses and forgives no one a wrong rhyme.

keepers.name: Kit Marlow
keepers.text: A young playwright with a quill sharper than most swords and enemies in every guildhall.

institutions.name: the Undercity Gate
institutions.title: Gatewarden
institutions.blurb: A warded gatehouse over the stair down into the cellars, the sewers and whatever lies under them. Its warden keeps a ledger of everyone who goes down and everyone who comes back, and the dark below stirs slower for it.

choice.label: what the Gatewarden does with the way down
choice.text: The council decides what the gate is for: keeping the dark in, letting the brave down, or letting the trade that already goes on below go on in the open.

options.name: bar it with iron
options.text: Iron grates, chains and a watch on every drain: little goes down, and less comes up.

options.name: license the delvers
options.text: Rat-catchers, treasure-hunters and green companies pay a fee to go down, and bring back salvage the warden taxes.

options.name: let the undermarket trade
options.text: The cellars host a night market the council pretends not to see. It pays, the Quiet Hand likes it, and it is noisy down there.

options.name: lanterns for the dead
options.text: A shrine at the foot of the stair, lamps along the old tunnels and prayers for whoever was buried down there: the town fears the dark a little less.

keepers.name: Brannoc Ironstair
keepers.text: A dwarf who counts the steps every morning in case one has gone missing. One did, once, and he will tell you about it.

keepers.name: Ysel Marrowdew
keepers.text: A former tomb-robber who knows every tunnel because she dug half of them, and who now charges others for what she used to do for free.

keepers.name: Father Ambrose Tull
keepers.text: An old priest of the dead who took the post nobody wanted. He talks to the dark below as if it might answer, and sometimes it does.

institutions.name: the Griffon Roost
institutions.title: Roostmaster
institutions.blurb: A timber tower of perches and nesting ledges where riders keep a flight of griffons. They wheel over the roads and the walls, and nothing sneaks up on a town that is watched from the sky.

choice.label: what the griffons fly for
choice.text: A flight of griffons can only be in one sky at a time. The council decides whose.

options.name: watching the roads
options.text: Riders sweep the trade roads at dawn and dusk: ambushers are seen from a mile off.

options.name: guarding the walls
options.text: The flight circles the town: raiders find griffons stooping on them before they reach the gate.

options.name: carrying the post
options.text: Letters, writs and small parcels by griffon to every town within a day's flight: merchants pay well for speed.

options.name: breeding foals
options.text: The roost raises foals and sells them to lords and companies who can afford them.

keepers.name: Hesk Windrow
keepers.text: A one-eyed rider who lost the other to a griffon he still flies. He says it was a fair trade.

keepers.name: Maudry Featherstone
keepers.text: She talks to the griffons in a whistled language no one else understands, and to people as little as possible.

keepers.name: Tamsin Gale
keepers.text: The youngest roostmaster the marches ever named, who wins every argument by flying away from it.

institutions.name: the Harbour
institutions.title: Harbourmaster
institutions.blurb: The quay, the slip and the net sheds, run by a harbourmaster who knows every boat and every tide. The town's ships fish from it and sail from it.

choice.label: what the quay is for first
choice.text: There is only so much quay, and the harbourmaster wants to know who gets it.

options.name: the fishing fleet
options.text: The boats go out on every tide and the smokehouses never cool: the moored ships land more fish.

options.name: merchant ships
options.text: Foreign hulls tie up and pay their dues; the quay pays its own way, and the town's own runs sell dearer.

options.name: a guard boat
options.text: A boat with a crossbow crew rows the harbour mouth all night: corsairs who come for the harbour meet it first.

keepers.name: Morwen Tarrant
keepers.text: Thirty years a pilot, she can name a ship by the set of its sails at a league.

keepers.name: Dobbin Strake
keepers.text: A retired corsair who says he knows how they think. Nobody asks how he retired.

keepers.name: Hesk Ollander
keepers.text: A dwarf who distrusts the sea completely and so checks every mooring twice.

institutions.name: the Sky Dock
institutions.title: Dockmaster
institutions.blurb: A mooring mast, a gasbag shed and a crew of gnome riggers who keep the town's airships flying. A company sails out in one straight over whatever water or mountain stands in the way, and is carried home again.

choice.label: who the airship sails for first
choice.text: The riggers need the council to say what the airships are for between voyages.

options.name: the companies
options.text: The airship waits on the companies' word: the hall fills with heroes who want a ride.

options.name: a lookout over the town
options.text: Between voyages it rides at anchor high over the walls: raiders are seen a day before they come.

options.name: paying passengers
options.text: Merchants and pilgrims pay well to fly over the mountains: the dock pays its own way.

keepers.name: Pell Quickwhistle
keepers.text: A gnome rigger who lost two airships and a brother to storms and still sails into every one he sees, singing.

keepers.name: Agathe Roul
keepers.text: Once a river pilot, she flies the airship like a barge: slowly, carefully and swearing at anything in the way.

keepers.name: Jorvin Tallow
keepers.text: He built his first gasbag from a hundred sewn pig bladders. The town still tells the story; he tells it differently.

institutions.name: the Monster Sanctuary
institutions.title: Beastwarden
institutions.blurb: Walled pens, deep pools and a great iron aviary where wounded or orphaned monsters are kept, studied and sometimes healed. The town both loves and fears it, and visitors come from far away to stare.

choice.label: what the sanctuary is for
choice.text: A cage full of monsters can be a school, a show, a hospital or a garrison. The council decides which.

options.name: study
options.text: Scholars draw and dissect: their notes make remedies from venoms and hides.

options.name: a menagerie for visitors
options.text: Ticketed walks past the pens: crowds, coin, and the odd fainting.

options.name: healing and release
options.text: Beasts are mended and let go far from the roads: the wilds are a little kinder to the town.

options.name: trained guardians
options.text: The tamest beasts are trained to guard the gates. Raiders do not like what they find there.

keepers.name: Corvane Ashby
keepers.text: A former monster-hunter who stopped killing them after he raised an owlbear cub by mistake. He still has the scars, and the owlbear.

keepers.name: Ildra Venn
keepers.text: A scholar who keeps meticulous records of every bite she has ever received, and is on her third ledger.

keepers.name: Gutch
keepers.text: A half-orc of few words and enormous patience, who can calm a basilisk by humming and has never explained how.

institutions.name: the Auction House of Marrow Lane
institutions.title: Auctioneer
institutions.blurb: A grand, gloomy hall where relics from ruins and dead adventurers' estates go under the hammer. The prices are excellent. Some of the lots are cursed. The auctioneer will not say which.

choice.label: the house's terms of sale
choice.text: Every lot carries a risk. The council decides how the house deals with it.

options.name: buyer beware
options.text: No questions, no guarantees, no refunds: the best prices and the worst surprises.

options.name: every lot appraised
options.text: A wizard checks every lot before the hammer falls: fewer curses, smaller profits.

options.name: sealed lots for the brave
options.text: Cursed lots are sold sealed to buyers who sign a waiver: adventurers love it.

options.name: a private room
options.text: A back room for buyers who prefer not to be seen: the Quiet Hand is a regular.

keepers.name: Silas Marrow
keepers.text: Gaunt, courteous and always in mourning black, he has sold three cursed crowns and never once touched one himself.

keepers.name: Madame Orsolya Vey
keepers.text: A dealer in antiquities who speaks of every lot as if it were a living person, which on occasion it is.

keepers.name: Pim Tallowby
keepers.text: A cheerful halfling with a hammer, a ledger and a remarkable talent for not being in the room when something goes wrong.

institutions.name: the Fey Market
institutions.title: Market Warden
institutions.blurb: On moonlit nights a market of stalls that were not there by day: fey traders selling bottled laughter, glass apples and luck by the ounce. Everything has a price, and not all prices are paid in coin.

choice.label: the market's rules
choice.text: The fey will trade on whatever terms the town sets, and keep to the letter of them. The council writes the letter.

options.name: coin only
options.text: No bargains for names, years or firstborns: honest trade, at fey prices.

options.name: any bargain freely made
options.text: Townsfolk may trade what they like. Most get the better of it. Some do not.

options.name: revels at the full moon
options.text: Music, dancing and lanterns on the water: the town loves it, and works a little less the morning after.

options.name: glamours for the town
options.text: The fey spin glamours over the streets: the town looks finer than it is, and settlers come.

keepers.name: Old Nettle
keepers.text: A townswoman who once bargained with a fey lord and won, and has been the only person they will deal with since.

keepers.name: Lirael of the Hollow Hill
keepers.text: A fey courtier exiled for reasons she finds hilarious, who keeps order with a smile no one wants to see twice.

keepers.name: Jory Blackthorn
keepers.text: A tinker who has spent too many nights in the market and now sees the stalls by day, which bothers him less than you would think.

institutions.name: the Oracle's Observatory
institutions.title: Oracle
institutions.blurb: A domed tower of brass and glass where the oracle reads stars, smoke and bones. Some of what she sees comes true. The trick is knowing which.

choice.label: what the oracle watches
choice.text: Even an oracle can only watch one sky at a time. The council decides which way she looks.

options.name: the town's enemies
options.text: She reads the stars for war and treachery: the walls are manned before the enemy comes.

options.name: harvests and weather
options.text: She tells the farmers when to sow and reap: the fields bear more.

options.name: the markets
options.text: She tells the merchants which caravans will come and which will not: the town trades shrewdly.

options.name: the will of the gods
options.text: She reads omens for the temples: the faithful are comforted, and the gods take note.

keepers.name: Sibyl Auremont
keepers.text: Blind since birth and unbothered by it, she says the stars are louder than they look.

keepers.name: Kestrel Duskwater
keepers.text: A former navigator who reads the sky like a chart and hates being asked about love.

keepers.name: The Veiled One
keepers.text: No one in town has seen her face. She answers questions before they are asked, which makes conversation brief.

institutions.name: the Delve
institutions.title: Delvemaster
institutions.blurb: Diggers under the town broke into a buried hall of the Stonekings: stair below stair of giant-cut stone, sealed doors and older things behind them. A shaft, a winch and a ledger now stand over it, and companies come from far away to go down.

choice.label: what the town does with the hall below
choice.text: A dungeon under the streets can make a town rich and famous, or eat it from below. The council decides how wide the way down stands.

options.name: seal it
options.text: Rubble, mortar and a ward over the shaft: the hall sleeps, and so does the town.

options.name: a guarded expedition gate
options.text: Licensed companies only, a watch on the winch and a rescue rope always ready: steady salvage, few surprises.

options.name: open to every company
options.text: Anyone with a lantern and a fee goes down. Coin, heroes and trouble all come up the shaft.

options.name: the town above the dungeon
options.text: Inns, guides, maps and souvenir giant-teeth: the dungeon becomes the town's name, and travellers come just to look.

keepers.name: Odda Ropeknot
keepers.text: A dwarf who has pulled more companies out of holes than anyone living, and bills them for the rope.

keepers.name: Senna Varlow
keepers.text: A retired cartographer who has mapped nine levels below and is sure there is a tenth, because the ninth has a door with no stair.

keepers.name: Bertil Hask
keepers.text: A former grave-digger who found the hall by accident and has been trying to make a living from it ever since.

institutions.name: the Embassy Quarter
institutions.title: Chamberlain
institutions.blurb: A walled square of envoys' houses: a dwarven reception hall half under the ground, a pavilion of living trees, and a flooded courtyard for guests who would rather swim. The Chamberlain keeps the peace between them, and the trade roads open wider for it.

choice.label: which embassy gets the best ground
choice.text: Every embassy wants the square's fountain at its door. The one that gets it brings the most.

options.name: the heirs of the Deep Realm
options.text: Dwarves and deep gnomes in a hall dug under the square: ore, tools and masons come up the roads.

options.name: the Court of First Leaves
options.text: Elven envoys in a pavilion of living boughs: herbs, timber and a little more patience in the town.

options.name: the stilt villages of the fens
options.text: Lizardfolk envoys in a flooded courtyard: fish, reeds and boatmen who know every river.

options.name: the free towns of the League
options.text: The League's old towns send merchants as envoys: another trade road and more coin on it.

keepers.name: Lord Aubric Fane
keepers.text: A courtier from a marcher house so old it has run out of land, who can insult anyone in eleven languages and never does.

keepers.name: Mirela Quent
keepers.text: A former smuggler who knows every envoy's secrets because she used to carry them.

keepers.name: Tobbe Underhill
keepers.text: A halfling who believes any quarrel can be ended with the right dinner, and has the kitchen to prove it.

institutions.name: the Gatehouse of Ways
institutions.title: Warden of Ways
institutions.blurb: A ring of black stone taller than the walls, raised on the pattern of the old Ashkaari gates, that opens on places no road reaches. What comes through is rich, strange and sometimes hungry, and the Warden of Ways decides which door stands open.

choice.label: which way the gate opens
choice.text: The ring can be tuned to one far place at a time. Each sends its own goods, visitors and trouble.

options.name: the Brass Shore
options.text: A coast of burning sand where salamander smiths work metal in the open air: tools and fire-hardened stone.

options.name: the Sung City
options.text: A city where every agreement must be sung. Its merchants pay in silver notes, and the town learns to hum.

options.name: the Hall of Hours
options.text: A quiet place of bells and white stone where the hurt are mended: pilgrims, healers and calmer nights.

options.name: keep it dark
options.text: The ring is left cold and warded. Nothing comes through, and nothing pays.

keepers.name: Ishmar Tey
keepers.text: A scholar of the old Ashkaari gates who has been through nine of them and back out of eight.

keepers.name: Dame Corisande Vell
keepers.text: A former knight of the League who guards the ring with a sword and a ledger, and trusts neither.

keepers.name: Pell
keepers.text: A small, very old being of uncertain origin who came through the ring the day it was finished and has been helpful ever since.

institutions.name: the Hall of Heroes
institutions.title: Curator
institutions.blurb: A long, high hall of trophies, memorial stones and recovered relics, with the town's adventures painted on its walls. Retired heroes teach in its yard, visitors come to stare, and one pedestal near the door stands empty, waiting for the founding banner the town lost long ago.

choice.label: what the hall honours first
choice.text: A hall of heroes can be a museum, a memorial, a school or a seat of old champions. The council decides which.

options.name: trophies and relics
options.text: Monster heads, broken crowns and a dragon's tooth the size of a door: travellers pay to see them.

options.name: the fallen
options.text: Memorial stones and candles for every hero who died for the town: the town mourns, and fears less.

options.name: a school for heroes
options.text: Retired heroes train the young in the yard, and more of them stay on in the town.

options.name: a seat of old champions
options.text: Grey-haired heroes sit as a council of their own, and stand on the walls when it matters.

keepers.name: Old Marta Greyhand
keepers.text: A retired sellsword who lost a hand to a troll and keeps it, pickled, in the first case by the door.

keepers.name: Fennick Dawe
keepers.text: A bard who never adventured, knows every hero's story better than they do, and corrects them.

keepers.name: Sir Hallam Brook
keepers.text: A knight who outlived his whole company and now dusts their shields every morning, one by one.

institutions.name: the Dragon's Eyrie
institutions.title: Dragon
institutions.blurb: A dragon has taken the old tower on the hill as its residence, by treaty. It guards the town, eats a great deal, collects things, and has opinions about all of them. Roofs are built steeper now, festivals have a dragon in them, and children dare each other to wave.

choice.label: the dragon's duties under the treaty
choice.text: The treaty names what the dragon does for the town in return for its tower, its meat and its collection.

options.name: protector
options.text: It circles the walls at dusk and the roads at dawn. Raiders who see it turn round.

options.name: scholar
options.text: It reads in the library by night and lectures by day. Scribes copy what it remembers from the age of giants.

options.name: patron
options.text: It lends from its hoard at a dragon's interest and invests in the town's trades.

options.name: a sociable neighbour
options.text: It attends every feast, judges the bake-off and gives rides at midsummer. Visitors come from three counties.

keepers.name: Verdigrael
keepers.text: A green-bronze dragon of great age who left the brood of the Old Wyrm, and says it was the best decision of its first thousand years.

keepers.name: Ossira Cinderwing
keepers.text: A young red dragon who wants very much to be admired, and has found that a town admires better than a village burns.

keepers.name: Haldrex Greyquill
keepers.text: A silver-grey dragon who came for the library, stayed for the bread, and keeps a list of everyone who has ever been rude to it.

institutions.name: the Monastery of the Falling Water
institutions.title: Abbot
institutions.blurb: A walled cloister round a courtyard where a stream falls from the upper terrace into a still pool. Its monks keep the hours, teach the open-hand forms to anyone who will rise at dawn, and send their best out into the world to see what they are made of.

choice.label: what the cloister teaches
choice.text: The brothers and sisters can only keep one discipline above the others. The council is asked which the town needs most.

options.name: the way of stillness
options.text: Quiet hours in the courtyard for anyone who comes: tempers cool, and those near breaking find their feet.

options.name: the way of the open hand
options.text: The forms taught at dawn in the square: more young folk take the road as monks, and the watch learns to fight without steel.

options.name: the way of the herb garden
options.text: The infirmary and its herb beds open to the town: wounds close, and nobody is turned away.

keepers.name: Abbot Tamsel Ure
keepers.text: A former mercenary captain who walked in out of the rain thirty years ago and never walked out. He still counts the gate guards when he passes them.

keepers.name: Mother Ildra Fenwise
keepers.text: She speaks perhaps a dozen words a day and makes every one of them land. The council dreads her visits and always does what she asks.

keepers.name: Brother Oswy Keld
keepers.text: Young, cheerful and alarmingly strong, he became abbot when the last one walked into the mountains and did not come back. He thinks she is still up there, thinking.

fixtures.name: a mimic for a bouncer
fixtures.text: A young mimic sits by the tavern door as a strongbox. Troublemakers who sit on it once never come back.

fixtures.name: a mimic strongbox
fixtures.text: The hall's strongbox has teeth. Nothing has been stolen since.

fixtures.name: a temple's guardian chest
fixtures.text: A mimic, blessed and fed on offerings, guards the reliquary. The priests say it purrs at hymns.

fixtures.name: the living bridge
fixtures.text: Willow and ash grown into a bridge over the river. Carts cross it, children climb it, and it grows a little every spring.

fixtures.name: the pilgrims' hostel
fixtures.text: A long hall of cots beside the temple for those who walk to it. Some stay.

fixtures.name: the oak in the square
fixtures.text: The awakened oak that walked to the market square, and stayed. It shades the stalls and settles arguments by dropping acorns.

fixtures.name: the trophy wall
fixtures.text: Heads, horns and a manticore's tail over the hall's hearth. Young heroes come to see it.

fixtures.name: the spice garden
fixtures.text: Seeds from a far caravan, coaxed into a walled garden behind the bazaar. Its pepper sells for silver.

fixtures.name: the oath-stone
fixtures.text: A standing stone in the chapterhouse yard where the town's oaths are sworn. Few lie with a hand on it.

fixtures.name: everburning lamps
fixtures.text: Glass globes of cold alchemical light along the main street, gifts of a grateful quarter.

fixtures.name: the brass gatekeeper
fixtures.text: A clockwork sentinel at the gate that never sleeps and never takes a bribe.

fixtures.name: the champion's statue
fixtures.text: A bronze of the town's greatest arena champion, polished bright by the hands of every child who touches it for luck.

fixtures.name: the town's anthem
fixtures.text: A song written for the town that every child knows by heart and every traveller carries away.

fixtures.name: a warning bell below
fixtures.text: A bell hung at the bottom of the stair, rung by whatever tries to pass. The watch is down there before it stops swinging.

fixtures.name: a tamed ooze in the sewers
fixtures.text: A great clear ooze that the warden feeds on rubbish. The sewers have never been cleaner, and nothing small lives down there any more.

fixtures.name: a griffon weathervane
fixtures.text: A great bronze griffon on the roost's peak that turns before every storm. The farmers swear by it.

fixtures.name: a dragon's egg
fixtures.text: A warm, humming egg in a nest of coals. The whole town is waiting to see what hatches.

fixtures.name: the iron box
fixtures.text: A lead-lined vault where cursed lots wait to be appraised. Things inside it knock, but less than they used to.

fixtures.name: a mushroom ring
fixtures.text: A ring of white mushrooms in the market square that no one steps in. The fey keep their word more carefully near it.

fixtures.name: a great orrery
fixtures.text: A clockwork model of the heavens, its brass spheres turning slowly overhead. It is sometimes a day ahead of the sky.

fixtures.name: a great winch over the shaft
fixtures.text: A counterweighted winch that lowers whole companies and hauls them back up, wounded or not.

fixtures.name: a giant's door in the square
fixtures.text: A stone door three storeys high, hauled up from the deep and stood in the market square. Travellers come to stand in it.

fixtures.name: a pavilion of living trees
fixtures.text: The elven envoys' gift: a pavilion whose boughs grew into its roof overnight. Treaties signed under it tend to hold.

fixtures.name: the envoys' long table
fixtures.text: A table where every embassy dines once a month by treaty. Most quarrels end over the second course.

fixtures.name: a singing stone
fixtures.text: A stone from the Sung City that hums the terms of every deal made beside it. Nobody cheats within earshot.

fixtures.name: the founding banner
fixtures.text: The banner the town's founders carried, recovered and hung over the empty pedestal at last. The whole town turned out to see it raised.

fixtures.name: a wall of names
fixtures.text: A wall carved with the name of every hero who fell for the town. People leave flowers under the names they knew.

fixtures.name: a dragonfire beacon
fixtures.text: A stone bowl on the tower that the dragon lights when danger comes. Everyone within ten miles knows to bar the door.

fixtures.name: griffon hatchlings for the rescue riders
fixtures.text: Hatchlings raised at the sanctuary and trained at the roost, flying rescue for lost companies and caravans.

precedents.text: The town promised the grove the river would run clean
The town broke its promise to keep the river clean
The Quiet Hand was given a stall in the bazaar's back rows
The town gave a fallen knight a second chance
The town licenses every invention the foundry builds
The town promised its bards they may mock anyone
The town turned a blind eye to the market under the streets
The town honoured a bargain made with the fey
The town made the auction house refund a cursed lot
The town paid the dragon's tithe

requests.title: A strange sail at the quay

stages.text: A black-hulled ship with no flag has tied up at the end of the quay and asks for water and rope. {keeper} thinks her crew have the look of corsairs, and the fishwives agree.

success.text: Under the nets the watch finds a hold of stolen bells and a corsair chart. The crew are put off at sword point and the chart goes to the council.

failure.text: The search turns up nothing but salt fish, and the crew sail off cursing the town to every port on the coast.

options.label: Sell them what they ask, at a price

success.text: {keeperName} charges double for water and rope, and the ship slips out on the next tide.
A boat of crossbowmen rows out and the black ship stands off without a word.

failure.text: The black ship stands off, but two of the town's boats go missing that week.

ignored.text: The black ship is gone in the night, and so are the harbour's best coils of rope.

requests.title: The novice who will not speak

stages.text: A novice at the Monastery has taken a vow of silence and stood in the falling water for three days. {keeper} says the novice saw something on the road that no one should see, and will not say what. The town is uneasy.

options.label: Sit with the novice until they speak

success.text: On the fourth day the novice speaks: raiders camped by the old road, counting the farms. The watch thanks the cloister.

failure.text: The novice stays silent, and the town's whispers fill the silence with worse things.

options.label: Let {keeperName} handle it in the cloister's own way

success.text: The abbot sits beside the novice in the water. Neither speaks. On the seventh day both walk out, and the cloister is calmer for it.

ignored.text: The novice walks out of the gate one morning and is not seen again. The brothers do not talk about it.

stages.text: A gale is coming down off the hills, and the airship is tugging at the mast like a hooked fish. {keeper} wants every spare hand on the ropes, and the guildsmen want their apprentices back at their benches.

options.label: Send the apprentices to the ropes

success.text: Forty apprentices haul the airship down to its cradle and sit on the ropes until dawn. The riggers buy them all a drink.

failure.text: A rope parts and the ship drags across three roofs before it is caught. The guildsmen send the council the bill.

options.label: Let {keeperName} fly it out of the storm

success.text: The airship cuts loose and rides the gale over the hills, coming home at noon with a story the riggers will tell for years.

failure.text: The airship comes home two days later, half its gasbag in tatters and its crew thinner. Patching it costs a fortune.

options.label: Pay the guilds for their time

success.text: The guilds lend their apprentices for coin and the ship is held through the night.

ignored.text: The gale tears the gasbag shed off its posts, and the riggers spend a month rebuilding it.

stages.text: Forty pilgrims have walked to {institution} for the holy day, footsore and with nowhere to sleep. {keeper} asks the town to shelter them.

success.text: The council pays for a long hall of cots beside the temple. The pilgrims bless the town on their way home, and some never leave.

options.label: Ask the faithful to take them in

success.text: Spare rooms open all over town. The pilgrims go home full of the town's kindness.

failure.text: Doors stay shut. The pilgrims sleep in the temple porch, and {keeperName} sleeps beside them in protest.

success.text: You send them on to the next shrine with bread and a letter. {keeper} is cool about it, but understands.

failure.text: The pilgrims trudge on to another town. {keeperName} does not speak to the council for a week.

ignored.text: No one decides, and the pilgrims sleep in the street.

stages.text: The reliquary of {institution} has been forced in the night and its holiest relic is gone. {keeper} is beside themself, and {hero} has offered to help.

success.text: {heroName} tracks the thieves to a barge on the river and brings the relic home in triumph.

failure.text: The trail goes cold at the river. {heroName} comes back empty-handed and embarrassed.

options.label: Quietly buy it back from the Quiet Hand

success.text: A knock at midnight, a purse changes hands, and the relic is on the altar by dawn. Nobody asks how.

options.label: Have the priests pray for its return

success.text: Three days of vigil, and the relic is found on the temple steps, the thief weeping beside it.

failure.text: The vigil ends with nothing but sore knees.

ignored.text: The relic is never found. The faithful say the town did not care.

stages.text: {keeper} wants the town to keep the high holy day of {institution} with a procession, bonfires and a feast in the square.

success.text: Banners, music and roast oxen. The whole town turns out and the priests are hoarse with blessing.

failure.text: It rains on the procession and the wine runs short, but the god is honoured, after a fashion.

success.text: Bread, ale and a short procession. Everyone enjoys it, briefly.
{keeperName} agrees the treasury has better uses this year, and almost means it.

failure.text: {keeperName} leaves the council chamber white with anger.

ignored.text: The holy day passes with no feast, and the faithful notice.

requests.title: A holy well in the way

stages.text: Builders digging new foundations have struck an old holy well, sealed long ago. {keeper} wants work stopped and the well kept.

options.label: Keep the well and build around it

success.text: The well is cleaned and roofed. Townsfolk drink from it for luck.

failure.text: The builders curse every stone of the new line, and charge for it. The well is kept, at a price.

success.text: The well is filled in. The builders finish early, and {keeperName} calls it sacrilege from the pulpit.

options.label: Find the old rite to move its blessing

success.text: {keeperName} finds the words in an old book, and the blessing moves to the temple font. Everyone is satisfied.

failure.text: The rite goes wrong, the well floods the site and the builders down tools.

ignored.text: The argument drags on until the builders fill the well in anyway.

stages.text: {keeper} has {hero} free this week and two jobs on the slate: a look at {site}, or riding guard on the caravan road to {settlement}.

success.text: {heroName} comes back with a sketch map and a fistful of old coins. The way into {site} is known now.

failure.text: The ruin has been picked clean long since. The company comes back with nothing but dust.

success.text: The caravan gets through without a scratch, and {people} remember who sent the guard.

failure.text: The bandits slip past the company in the night, and the caravan limps in a wagon short.

success.text: {heroName} scouts {site} by night and rides with the caravan by day, and pulls it off.

failure.text: Trying to be in two places at once, {heroName} manages neither well and comes home bloodied.

ignored.text: The week goes by and {heroName} drinks it away at the hall.

stages.text: {hero}'s company and another have been at each other's throats over who cleared a ruin first. {keeper} wants the mayor to settle it before somebody is stabbed in the hall.

options.label: Make them race for the next bounty

success.text: Both companies sprint for the hills. The rivalry becomes the town's favourite sport.

failure.text: The race turns into a brawl on the north road.

success.text: A sharp word, a heavy fine, and peace returns.

failure.text: Nobody listens, and {keeperName} has to break up the fight with a chair.

options.label: Let them settle it in the yard

success.text: A bout in the hall's yard, cheered by half the town. {heroName} wins, bruised.

ignored.text: The quarrel festers, and both companies drink elsewhere for a while.

stages.text: {hero}'s company came home with gold, monster hide and a complication: an envoy of {people} at the hall's door, saying the ruin they looted was a burial ground of their ancestors.

success.text: Coin and an apology. {people} go home mollified.
You stand by the company, and argue it well enough that {people} grumble rather than rage.

failure.text: You stand by them, and {people} take it as a declaration. Their envoy stops coming to dinner.

options.label: Broker a ceremony to return what matters

success.text: The bones go home with honour, the gold stays. Everyone leaves satisfied.

failure.text: The talks collapse in shouting.

ignored.text: Nobody answers the envoy, who leaves in a cold fury.

stages.text: {party} are a week overdue. {keeper} wants to send a rescue company after them and asks the council to pay for it.

success.text: The rescuers find {party} holed up in a cave, hungry but alive, and bring them home to cheers.
A voice crackles back from the wilds: they are pinned down but holding. The hall breathes again.

failure.text: The stone stays silent. {keeperName} paces all night.

success.text: You say it at the hall, plainly, and pay for a lamp in the window. The companies grumble, but they knew.

failure.text: The council says so. {keeperName} says something worse.

ignored.text: No one goes. {party} will make it home or they won't.

stages.text: A trader in a fur hood has set up at {institution} with a crate of warm, speckled eggs. {keeper} wants to know whether the town will allow it.

options.label: Buy the clutch and sell the hatchlings on

success.text: The hatchlings fetch a fortune from a noble's menagerie.

failure.text: The eggs hatch early in the warehouse. It takes the watch two days to catch everything.

options.label: Let the trader sell, for a licence fee

success.text: A brisk trade in eggs, and a fat licence for the treasury.

failure.text: The trader pays a pittance and sells three hatchlings that bite. The bazaar is not amused.

success.text: The crate goes back on the cart. {keeperName} sighs at the lost fee.

ignored.text: The trader sells the eggs anyway, to whoever asks.

stages.text: Two caravans want the town's guard on the same road: a spice train bound for {institution}, and the town's own convoy to {settlement}. There are only enough riders for one.

success.text: The spices arrive safe and the bazaar does a week's trade in a day.

failure.text: The spice train gets through, short two wagons, and the council asks why it paid for the other caravan to go hungry.

success.text: The convoy gets through. {people} are pleased; {keeperName} is not.

failure.text: The convoy is raided anyway, and the bazaar is left to fend for itself as well.

success.text: Both get through, and the sellswords drink their pay at the bazaar.

ignored.text: Both caravans set out without guards and hope for the best.

stages.text: A soft-spoken woman from {faction} says they know of a smuggling ring working out of {institution}. They will name names, in exchange for a stall in the bazaar's restricted back rows.

success.text: The smugglers are taken in a night. The Hand gets its stall, and {keeperName} gets a new neighbour {keeperName} did not choose.

options.label: Refuse, and have the watch find the smugglers

success.text: Two weeks of patient watching, and the ring is broken without the Hand's help.

failure.text: The smugglers get wind of the watch and slip away.

options.label: Tell {keeperName} and let the bazaar deal with it

success.text: {keeperName} thanks the mayor, and the bazaar's porters see the smugglers out of town.

failure.text: {keeperName} thinks the mayor is accusing the bazaar, and takes offence.

ignored.text: The offer is withdrawn, and the smuggling goes on.

stages.text: A caravan from the far oasis cities has brought a chest of old books to {institution}: star charts, bestiaries, a grimoire with a lock on it. {keeper} has kept them back for the town to see first.

options.label: Buy them for the town's scholars

success.text: The books go to the town's shelves. The mayor reads late into the night, and learns something.

options.label: Let the Order of the Unshut Book bid

success.text: The Order outbids everyone and is delighted. The bazaar takes its cut.

failure.text: The Order bids low and gets them anyway; nobody else dares bid against it.

options.label: Have someone open the grimoire first

success.text: The lock gives, and the grimoire holds nothing worse than an alchemist's recipes. It sells for a good price.

failure.text: Something comes out of the grimoire, and it takes the town's priests a day to put it back.

ignored.text: The books are sold off a cart to whoever asks.

stages.text: The tanneries upstream are fouling the stream that feeds the grove's sacred pool. {keeper} wants them moved downstream.

success.text: New pits downstream, and the pool runs clear again.

options.label: Fine the tanners into cleaning up

success.text: The tanners grumble, pay and dig settling ponds.

failure.text: The tanners laugh at the fine and carry on.

options.label: Tell the druids to live with it

success.text: You promise the druids the tanneries will move when the town can afford it. They don't believe you, quite.

failure.text: The pool scums over. The druids say nothing, which is worse.

ignored.text: The stream stays foul and the pool sickens.

stages.text: The grove's oldest oak has woken and decided to move. It wants to stand in the market square, and is already halfway down the lane. {keeper} asks the mayor to clear it a way.

options.label: Clear it a path to the square

success.text: Stalls are moved and a wall comes down. The oak settles in the square with a long creak of contentment.

options.label: Persuade it to stay in the grove

success.text: A long, slow conversation at dawn. The oak agrees to stay, for another hundred years.

failure.text: The oak does not care for being argued with, and walks through the tanners' yard instead.

success.text: You find a fence it doesn't mind: willow, woven by the druids. It stays put, sulking.

failure.text: Chains and posts. The oak stops, and the grove goes very quiet.

ignored.text: The oak walks where it likes, and the town picks up the pieces.

stages.text: {keeper} offers to grow a living bridge of willow and ash across the river, on one condition: the river beneath it must be kept clean forever.

success.text: The druids sing to the saplings, and in a season a bridge stands where none did.

failure.text: The druids take the promise, but the bridge grows thin and slow, and they say the river can tell a half-meant oath.

options.label: Ask for a bridge without promises

success.text: {keeperName} considers it and agrees, on a smaller bridge.

failure.text: {keeperName} says a gift with no promise is a purchase, and the grove does not sell.

success.text: The council builds its own bridge of stone, later and dearer.

ignored.text: The offer withers on the bough.

stages.text: A dyer's vat has burst and the river below the living bridge runs blue. {keeper} reminds the mayor of the town's promise.

options.label: Pay for the river to be cleaned

success.text: Men with nets and buckets work for a week, and the river runs clear. The bridge puts out new leaves.
The dyer pays, and the river is cleaned.

failure.text: The dyer has nothing to pay with, and the river stays blue.

success.text: You make the druids see it washes out in a season. They don't like it, but it won't be the end of the world.

failure.text: The bridge withers on one side. The druids say the town's word is worth nothing.

ignored.text: No one cleans it up. The promise is broken.

stages.text: The spirits of the woods beyond the walls are furious with the woodcutters. Wolves follow the timber carts, and trees fall across the roads. {keeper} offers to parley for the town.

success.text: The spirits accept a bargain: the woodcutters plant two for every one they fell.

failure.text: The spirits will not listen, and the woods grow darker.

success.text: The woodcutters work fewer days and the woods settle.
The hunters thin the pack and bring back timber from the edge. The grove is cold about it.

failure.text: The hunters come back two wolves short and one man down, and the woods are quieter in the worst way.

ignored.text: The woods stay angry.

stages.text: {hero} would hang up the sword and buy a share of {institution} from {keeper}. There is a catch: old enemies have a way of following a hero to their door.

success.text: {heroName} buys in and pulls pints between delves. Business booms.
{heroName} agrees the wilds still need them, and stays on the road.

failure.text: {heroName} sulks for a week.

stages.text: A month later, a band of hard-faced strangers walks into {institution} and asks for {heroName} by an old name.

success.text: {heroName} meets them in the yard, and the strangers leave on stretchers. The tavern's fame doubles.

failure.text: The fight wrecks the taproom, and {heroName} is badly hurt.

success.text: A heavy purse and they ride away, promising nothing.
The watch takes them in before a blow is struck.

failure.text: The watch arrives late, to a broken taproom.

ignored.text: The strangers wait for {heroName} in the street, and it ends in blood.
{heroName} takes the silence as a no.

stages.text: A cloaked stranger has sat in the corner of {institution} for three nights, asking anyone who will listen for help with something buried at {site}. {keeper} thinks the mayor should hear it.

success.text: The stranger draws a map on the table in spilled ale and is gone by morning. The map is good.

failure.text: The stranger talks in riddles and leaves without paying.

success.text: A purse for a parchment. The map is old, but good.
Out they go, without a fuss. Nobody misses them.

failure.text: The stranger won't go quietly, and takes a table with them. The regulars are not pleased.

ignored.text: The stranger leaves town, and takes the story with them.

stages.text: {hero}'s company carried home a magnificent treasure chest. In the hall's strongroom it bit the clerk. It is a young mimic, and everyone in town has an idea what to do with it.

options.label: Give it to the tavern as a bouncer

success.text: The mimic takes to its new door at once. Brawls at the tavern end very quickly now.

failure.text: It bites the landlord on its first night and has to be chained in the cellar.

options.label: Let the temple bless and keep it

success.text: Fed on offerings and hymns, the mimic guards the reliquary like a hound.

failure.text: The blessing doesn't take. The priests keep it in the crypt, and sleep badly.

options.label: Let the Quiet Hand train it

success.text: The Hand's people take it away in a sack. Strongboxes across town start going missing, but never theirs.

options.label: Tame it as the hall's strongbox

success.text: It learns to open only for {keeperName}. The hall has never been safer.

failure.text: It does not want to be tamed, and {heroName} loses a fingertip finding out.

ignored.text: Nobody decides, and one morning the mimic is gone, along with a cartwheel.

stages.text: The priests of {institution2} want a bough of the grove's ancient tree for a new altar. {keeper} refuses: you do not cut a living elder to carve a dead one. Both come to the mayor.

success.text: The tree keeps its bough. The priests find oak elsewhere, sourly.

failure.text: You side with the grove, and the temple takes it as a slight on the god himself.

success.text: The bough is cut with great ceremony. The druids watch in silence.
The tree lets fall a bough of its own accord at a joint dawn rite. Both call it a miracle.

failure.text: The rite turns into a shouting match under the tree.

ignored.text: The quarrel rumbles on, and both blame the mayor.

stages.text: {hero} wants to sell a jewelled idol from the wilds at {institution2}. {keeper2} wants the bazaar's cut; {keeper} insists the hall's fee comes first. The idol sits on the council table between them.

success.text: The hall takes its fee and the bazaar sulks.

failure.text: The hall gets its fee, and the bazaar says it was robbed in daylight.

options.label: The bazaar sells it, the bazaar's cut

success.text: The bazaar takes its cut and the hall grumbles.
A public auction draws half the region. The idol fetches a fortune, and both keepers are paid.

failure.text: The auction draws thieves as well as buyers, and the idol vanishes in the crush.

ignored.text: {hero} sells it to a passing pedlar for half its worth.

stages.text: {hero}'s new ballad about the companies of {institution} is sung in every tavern on the road. Recruits are arriving, and so are challengers who want to test the town's heroes.

success.text: The ballad spreads. New faces fill the hall, and a few bloody noses with them.

failure.text: The fame brings the wrong sort: brawlers and chancers looking for a name of their own.

options.label: Ask for a verse about the town

success.text: {heroName} adds three verses about the town's walls and warm beds. Settlers come, not just swords.

failure.text: The new verses rhyme 'town' with 'drown'. Nobody sings them.

success.text: {heroName} is hurt, but sings something else.

ignored.text: The ballad goes where ballads go.

stages.text: {keeper} has noticed {faction} meeting in the back room of {institution} every Moonday, and wants to know whether the mayor would rather they did or didn't.

options.label: Let them meet there, and listen

success.text: {keeperName} keeps an ear to the wall. The town learns a great deal.

failure.text: They catch the listener in the rafters. The Hand is not pleased, and the tavern pays for it.

options.label: Let them meet, and leave them be

success.text: The Hand notices the courtesy.
{keeperName} turns them out with a smile and a cudgel.

failure.text: The Hand turns {keeperName}'s cellar out first. Barrels are broken.

ignored.text: The Hand keeps meeting, and nobody says anything.

requests.title: A book that will not come back to {institution}

stages.text: A spellbook borrowed from {institution} by a hedge-witch has not come back, and the witch has locked herself in her cottage with it. Odd lights show in her windows. {keeper} wants the council to act.

success.text: The witch takes the coin and hands the book over, a little singed. She asks if she may read in the library instead. She may.
She brings it back herself, with notes in the margins that the wizards find surprisingly useful.

failure.text: She slams the door. Next morning the book is back on its shelf, and every candle in the library has turned blue.

success.text: You make her promise to leave it to the library in her will. The librarians grumble, but accept it.

failure.text: The library writes the book off. {keeperName} writes the council a letter about it.

ignored.text: The lights in the witch's windows grow stranger, and the library's goodwill thins.

stages.text: One of {keeper}'s knights got drunk, drew steel on a carter and broke {choice}. The chapter would strip him of his spurs and drive him out; his family begs the mayor for mercy.

options.label: Let the chapter judge its own

success.text: The knight rides out of the gate at dawn without his spurs. The chapter is satisfied.

failure.text: The chapter whitewashes him, and the town notices.

success.text: {keeperName} grants it, grudgingly: the knight will serve a year as a squire again.

failure.text: {keeperName} will not hear of it, and resents being asked.

options.label: Have the town's court try him instead

success.text: The court fines him and lets him go. The knights mutter about civil men judging holy ones.

ignored.text: The chapter judges him without the mayor, and notes that the mayor did not care.

stages.text: {keeper} asks the council's blessing and purse for a crusade against {menace}. The knights would ride out within the week.

success.text: The knights ride out under the town's banner and return with {menace} bloodied and their ranks thinned.
The knights go anyway, fewer and poorer, and do what they can.

failure.text: Without coin the crusade never leaves the yard, and the knights blame the council.

options.label: Forbid it: the town needs them here

success.text: You make the knights see where the town's danger lies. They stay, sour but sworn.

failure.text: The knights stay and stand on the walls, sullen.

ignored.text: The knights wait for a blessing that never comes.

stages.text: {keeper} wants the great square for the chapter's vigil on the same night {keeper2} has promised it to the temple's procession. Both expect the mayor to settle it.

options.label: Give the square to the knights

success.text: The vigil is splendid, and the priests sulk in the side streets.

failure.text: The knights get the square, and the temple says so from the pulpit every week.

options.label: Give the square to the temple

success.text: The procession is glorious, and the knights stand guard at its edges, stone-faced.
Knights and priests keep the night together, and it becomes a festival the town remembers.

failure.text: Knights and priests spend the night arguing over precedence in front of everyone.

ignored.text: Both turn up, and the night ends with shoving.

stages.text: A still in {institution} has gone up in green fire and taken a neighbour's roof with it. The neighbours want the quarter moved outside the walls; {keeper} says it was an accident and will not happen again.

options.label: Pay for the roof and let them carry on

success.text: A new roof, a stern word, and the quarter goes back to work.
{keeperName} pays, with very bad grace.

failure.text: The quarter won't pay, and says so loudly. You end up with neither the gold nor the goodwill.

options.label: Order stone walls between the stills

success.text: The quarter grumbles and builds them. Nothing has burned since.

failure.text: The walls go up in the wrong places, and the alchemists have to knock half of them through.

ignored.text: The neighbours take the matter into their own hands, and the quarter's windows are broken.

stages.text: {keeper} needs the heart of a beast from {site} for a great work, and offers the council a share of what comes of it.

success.text: The heart arrives in a bucket of ice, and the quarter's great work bubbles for a month.
{keeperName} goes, and comes back singed but triumphant.

failure.text: {keeperName} comes back without it, and without an eyebrow.

success.text: You point {keeperName} to a cheaper reagent in an old herbal. It isn't the same, but it'll do.

failure.text: The great work waits.

ignored.text: The great work waits.

stages.text: The alchemists want to harvest the moonpetal that grows only in the druids' sacred pool. {keeper} offers good coin; {keeper2} says the pool is not for sale.

success.text: The moonpetal stays. The alchemists find a substitute that works almost as well.

failure.text: You side with the grove, and the alchemists say the town has chosen weeds over gold.

success.text: The petals are harvested, the potions are superb, and the druids do not forgive it.
The druids harvest a few petals each full moon, and sell them dear. Both sides are grudgingly content.

failure.text: Neither side will budge, and both blame the mayor.

ignored.text: The alchemists harvest by night, and the druids catch them at it.

stages.text: One of {keeper}'s clockwork labourers has wandered out of {institution} and is carrying a market stall, very carefully, towards the river.

options.label: Send the watch to stop it

success.text: Six watchmen and a net bring it down. The stall survives; the watchmen are bruised.

failure.text: The automaton walks into the river, stall and all. The stallholder wants paying.

success.text: {keeperName} whistles a long, odd tune, and it puts the stall down and walks home.

failure.text: {keeperName}'s tune makes it walk faster.

success.text: Hammers make short work of it. {keeperName} weeps over the parts.

ignored.text: The automaton reaches the river and keeps walking. It is still down there.

stages.text: Two of the foundry's artificers swear they invented the same self-stoking furnace. {keeper} wants the council to grant one a licence and settle it.

options.label: Grant licences on the council's terms

success.text: From now on, every invention is licensed by the town, for a fee. The artificers grumble and pay.

failure.text: The licences are granted, but the terms please nobody and the foundry sulks.

success.text: They hate each other, and the furnace is the best ever built.

failure.text: They burn the first one down arguing over the flue.

success.text: {keeperName} settles it by giving the furnace to a third artificer entirely.

ignored.text: The quarrel goes on for months.

stages.text: {keeper} has learned that the town's library holds a dwarven book of schematics, and wants it lent to the foundry. The librarians say it is far too old to leave the reading room.

success.text: The schematics come back oily and dog-eared, and the foundry builds something marvellous from them.

failure.text: The librarians lend the book with the important pages missing. The foundry builds nothing from it.

success.text: A careful copy goes to the foundry; the original stays safe. The gatekeeper they build from it stands at the gate to this day.
You side with the librarians, but find the foundry a lesser book to work from. It helps a little.

failure.text: The book stays where it is. {keeperName} is not pleased.

ignored.text: {keeperName} tries to borrow it without asking, and is caught.

stages.text: A champion from the south has beaten every fighter in {institution} and now calls out {hero} by name before the whole crowd. {keeper} says the town's honour is on the line.

success.text: {heroName} wins in the fourth bout, and the crowd carries them through the streets.

failure.text: {heroName} loses badly and limps off to jeers.

success.text: The crowd boos, and {keeperName} has to give back half the gate.
The fight is thrilling and the result never in doubt. Only {keeperName} knows.

failure.text: The champion takes the gold and falls over far too soon. The crowd smells the fix.

ignored.text: The southern champion claims the town has no heroes, and the crowd half believes it.

requests.title: A beast loose from the pens

stages.text: An owlbear has broken out of the arena's pens and is loose in the streets. {keeper} swears the bars were sound.

success.text: The watch corners it in a bakery, with losses on both sides.

failure.text: The watch flees, and the owlbear eats the bakery's stock and goes back to its pen of its own accord.

success.text: {heroName} drives it back into the pen with a torch and a lot of shouting.

failure.text: {heroName} is mauled, and the beast is killed.

options.label: Close the arena's pens for good

success.text: No more beasts in the arena. The crowds are smaller.

ignored.text: The owlbear rampages for a night before the watch kills it.

stages.text: The college's new play is about a vain, greedy mayor who looks remarkably like the real one. The town loves it. {keeper} waits to see what the mayor will do.

success.text: The mayor attends opening night and laughs loudest. The town warms to them.

failure.text: Your laugh comes a beat late and the whole house sees it. The play goes on, and so does the joke.

options.label: Ask for the worst lines to be cut

success.text: {keeperName} cuts them, and the cut lines become the town's favourite jokes.

failure.text: {keeperName} refuses, loudly, on stage.

success.text: The play closes. Everyone hears about it, and everyone takes the bards' side.

ignored.text: The play runs for months, and nobody hears the mayor's side.

stages.text: {keeper} wants to write the hall's great ballad, but {keeper2} insists it be about {hero} and get every detail right. The bards say the truth is never as good as the song.

success.text: The ballad is magnificent and largely invented. {heroName} is famous for things they never did.

failure.text: The bards embellish it so far that the companies in the hall laugh out loud at the dragon in the third verse.

success.text: The ballad is shorter, and the hall's companies love it.
{heroName} tells it in the taproom, and the bards scribble. The ballad is honest and stirring.

failure.text: {heroName} stammers through it, and the bards fill in the gaps.

ignored.text: The bards write it anyway, and the hall hates it.

stages.text: A travelling troupe has set up in the square and is drawing the college's crowds. {keeper} asks the council to move them on.

success.text: The troupe moves on, and the college's benches fill again.

failure.text: The rival troupe goes, but plays its last night in the square for free, and draws the bigger crowd.

success.text: The two companies stage a festival of plays together, and the town talks of nothing else.

failure.text: The two companies hate each other on sight.

success.text: The troupe stays a month and the college sulks.

ignored.text: The troupe stays, and the college sulks.

stages.text: Something is knocking on the inside of the old door at the bottom of the gate's stair, slow and patient, every night. {keeper} wants to know whether the council would rather open it or brick it up.

success.text: The watch opens it on something that was waiting a long time and was not ready for spears. {site} is quieter for it.

failure.text: The door opens and the watch runs. Whatever was knocking is out in the tunnels now.

options.label: Ask a hero to open it

success.text: {heroName} opens it, goes through, and comes back an hour later with a broken blade and a story. The knocking stops.

failure.text: {heroName} comes back up bleeding and will not say what was behind it.

success.text: Three courses of brick and a ward chalked on them. The knocking goes on, fainter.

ignored.text: One night the knocking stops. Nobody knows which side of the door it is on now.

stages.text: The sewer men have found a great clear ooze eating its way along the drains. {keeper} thinks it could be fed on rubbish and kept, like a dog; the sewer men want it burned.

success.text: {keeperName} coaxes it into the old cistern with a cart of offal. The sewers are cleaner than they have been in a hundred years.

failure.text: It eats the cart, the offal and a sewer man's boots, with the sewer man still in them for a moment.

success.text: The drains stink of it for a week, and the warden sulks.
An alchemist pays well for it and asks whether there are more.

failure.text: Nobody wants it at the asking price. It goes for a pittance to a man who doesn't say what for.

ignored.text: Left alone, it eats the sewer grates and wanders into a cellar.

stages.text: Two traders in the undermarket came to knives over a crate nobody will name. One is dead, the watch wants to go down in force, and {keeper} says the market only works if the watch stays above.

success.text: The market settles its own quarrel, quietly. {keeperName} sends up a purse and a nod.

failure.text: The undermarket takes the blind eye as a licence, and things come up the stair that shouldn't.

success.text: The watch takes the crate and the killer. The market moves deeper, and the warden's ledger has gaps now.

options.label: Find out what was in the crate

success.text: A sealed reliquary out of {site}. The killer is taken quietly, and the reliquary goes to the temple.

failure.text: The crate is gone by the time anyone asks.

ignored.text: The market buries its dead in the tunnels and opens again the next night.

stages.text: Diggers have broken into a forgotten burial vault in {site}. {keeper2} wants the bones raised and buried again with every rite; {keeper} wants the vault sealed before what lies there notices the light.

success.text: A long procession of bones goes up the stair by lamplight, and the town's dead rest easier. So does the town.

failure.text: Something in the vault does not want to be moved. Priests come up running, and the bones are left where they fell.

success.text: Mortar, iron and a ward of the warden's own. The priests call it a second burial without rites.

failure.text: The seal cracks within the month, and the priests say they told you so.

options.label: Bless the vault and leave the dead in it

success.text: Priests and warden go down together, and the vault is blessed where it lies. Both grumble, neither refuses.

ignored.text: No one decides, and the diggers fill the hole back in themselves. Lights are seen down there at night.

stages.text: {keeper2} wants the hall's companies to take delving contracts in {site}, paid by the hall and logged at the gate. {keeper} says green companies going down for coin is how the dark gets fed.

success.text: Companies queue at the gate with lanterns and fresh rope. Most come back, richer.

failure.text: The hall posts its contracts, and the first company down comes up short a man. The Gatewarden is furious.

success.text: The warden checks every company's ledger at the stair. Fewer go down, and fewer stay there.

failure.text: Every chancer in the hall swears they are a veteran, and the Gatewarden can't tell the difference.

options.label: Keep the way down shut to companies

success.text: The hall's companies go back to the road, muttering about the warden.

ignored.text: Companies go down anyway, without contracts or a ledger, and not all of them come back.

stages.text: {keeper} has found a tunnel from the old cellars running straight into {keeper2}'s cellar under the famous tavern, worn smooth by feet and barrels. Neither will say who dug it.

success.text: The tunnel is bricked at both ends. The tavern's ale gets dearer, and {keeper2} will not look the warden in the eye.

failure.text: The masons brick it up badly, and the cellar floods the first time it rains.

options.label: Let it be: it is a tavern

success.text: The barrels keep rolling. The warden writes it in the ledger and underlines it twice.
At the far end the watch finds a smugglers' cache, and the council a nice share of it.

failure.text: The tunnel branches, and branches again, and the watch comes back up lost and empty-handed.
